FSUK Sim Racing Series 2025–26 · Finals

A glimpse from
Williams F1 HQ

Last season, Formula IUT took its drivers and race engineers all the way to the FSUK Sim Racing Series finals at Williams F1 headquarters in Grove, UK. We finished P9 in the Engineering Challenge and P9 in Finals B.

Next season, this could be you.

We want to see you in the team soon. Good luck with the tasks — we can’t wait to read your report.

We do not expect you to know all the answers, or even the right ones. We want to see your curiosity: how you attack a problem you have never faced, and how you use AI and the internet to learn.

Most of what you read here will be new to you, and that is expected. Search it up online, study it, and write your report from what you learned. Show us how you think, where you got stuck and what you did about it. This is exactly what the Formula Student UK engineering challenges reward. We will hold a viva and ask questions based on your report, so write only what you understand and can explain.

For race drivers and race engineers. This evaluation applies to both. These are the basics that build the bridge between a driver and an engineer, so both sides need to speak the same language. Race drivers are not expected to go as deep into the topics. Aim for a clear understanding of the ideas and the ability to describe them well.
  • Use AI as a tutor, not a ghostwriter.Ask it to explain concepts, check your logic and challenge your choices. Then write the answer in your own words.
  • Give a direction and a reason.Say what you would change, by how much, what it does to the car and which telemetry channel would prove it.
  • Change one thing at a time.If you change several parameters in one scenario, explain why they cannot be separated.
  • Say what could go wrong.Every change costs something somewhere else on the lap. Name it.
  • Be honest about limits.A sim can behave differently from textbook theory. If you are unsure, say so and say how you would test it.

The seven tasks

These questions are prepared to match the requirements of the engineering challenges in the Formula Student UK Sim Racing Series. Complete all seven and answer every question. Tick a question as you finish it to track your progress. Ticks are saved in this browser only.

Study guide

The basics of race engineering and car dynamics. Read a topic, search every term you do not know, then try to explain it in your own words.

MoTeC data

Task 6 uses a real lap from Formula IUT's lead driver, driven in the 2025/26 Formula Student UK season. Download the pack, open it in MoTeC i2 and analyse the lap.

  1. Install MoTeC i2. The free version is enough. Follow this installation video on YouTube, then search for a beginner tutorial if you have never used it.
  2. Unzip both files into one folder. Keep the .ld and the .ldx side by side. The .ldx carries the lap markers.
  3. Open the .ld file in i2. Pick a lap and plot channels against distance to begin.

Want a deeper walkthrough? Watch the detailed MoTeC explanation playlist on YouTube. It is not mandatory.

Submit your report

When all seven tasks are done, send your report through the Google Form. You will need your report as a single PDF.

Open the submission form

After you submit, there will be a viva where we ask questions based on your report. Be ready to explain any answer, plot or setup decision out loud, without notes, and to say what you would do differently.

  • One PDF, no more than 6 pages. Write your name, student ID, department and contact number at the top of the first page, and state whether you are applying as a race driver, race engineer or both.
  • All seven tasks answered, every question covered.
  • Short, scannable writing: bullets, small tables and simple sketches.
  • Your own words, with honest notes on what you were unsure about.
  • For Task 5, the one-page driver and engineer aid. For Task 6, your plots with annotations. For Task 7, your meme and its short explanation on the last page.

How we mark

CategoryMarksWhat we look for
Engineering reasoning10Correct physics, sensible direction and size of changes, awareness of trade-offs
Setup decisions10Clear choice of what to change first, one change at a time, a plan to verify
Communication10Clear, concise, easy to scan, plain words, useful sketches or tables
Own voice and honesty5Answers in your own words, uncertainty admitted, no copy-paste
Curiosity5Good questions, extra ideas, links to what you saw in real or sim racing
